13833.title: WIRED Newsletters blocked as spam
13833.note: 550 5.7.1 comes from ImprovMX's MX (SpamAssassin, hard 5.0 cutoff, build v2026.09.11); the mail never reaches newsletter_receive. mtaylor's WIRED feed 10067048 got a story daily through Sep 11, none since. UPDATE 2026-09-13T23:19:55Z: ImprovMX support replied that the filter cannot be changed per domain, but a webhook destination can append ?spam_check=false to skip it. Sam adds that in the ImprovMX dashboard on the newsletters.newsblur.com catch-all alias (route ^receive/?$ ignores the query string, verified). ImprovMX also flagged DMARC: there is no _dmarc.newsletters.newsblur.com TXT at all (DNS is at DNSimple); v=DMARC1; p=none is enough. Replies assume the dashboard change is done.
13833.reply: Found the cause and fixed it. That bounce was coming from ImprovMX, the service that receives mail for newsletters.newsblur.com and hands it to NewsBlur. They pushed an update on September 11 and their spam scoring started putting some WIRED emails right at the 5.0 cutoff, so the message was rejected before it ever reached NewsBlur. Your WIRED feed was getting a story every day through the 11th and then stopped, which matches. ImprovMX gave me a way to skip their spam check for mail headed to NewsBlur, since every newsletter address already has a secret token in it, and that's now on. The next WIRED email should come through. Let me know if it doesn't.

13832.title: TMZ feed not updating for the last few days
13832.note: Follow-up: kblackwell says the feed is back (they read branch feed 10310518, fetched via proxy) but no images. TMZ's RSS has never carried images; text and thumbnails came from Text view fetches of article pages, which TMZ 403s from Hetzner (Mercury on hnode-text and direct both verified). TextImporter had no proxy fallback; PageImporter did. Sam chose the PR: TextImporter falls back to ScrapingBee on blocked responses (403/429/503 or a 200 challenge page), source original_text, host daily cap honored; PageImporter shares the detection. Six Codex rounds (Sam chose to run past the three-round cap), all resolved. Reply assumes deploy. ScrapingBee at 97.4% used, 27K credits left to Sep 30. 13832.reply: Found the cause of the missing images. TMZ's feed itself only carries a one-paragraph summary, no pictures. The text and images you were seeing came from NewsBlur loading the full article page for Text view and pulling its lead image for the thumbnail, and TMZ now blocks those article-page requests from our servers the same way it blocked the feed. I've wired Text view through the same proxy the feed uses, so the full text and images will come back in the next deploy. Stories already in the feed pick it up the next time you open them in Text view.

13827.title: Is there any way to stop any Google News Stories
13827.note: news.google.com/rss/articles/<token> links redirect to consent.google.com from NewsBlur's EU servers and the consent page was extracted as story text. Fix: Feed.resolve_google_redirect_url decodes the token via MStory._decode_google_news_url; TextImporter refuses consent.google.com; fetch_original_text drops cached consent text. Verified decoder works from happ-web-01. Reply assumes deploy (make deploy + make celery).
13827.reply: JTTraveler is right that Google News feeds only carry a headline and a link, but that cookie notice was on NewsBlur's side. Google News links go through a news.google.com redirect, and when NewsBlur's servers, which sit in Europe, followed it to pull the article text, Google handed them its cookie consent page instead of the story. That page is what ended up as the text. I've fixed it so NewsBlur decodes the link to the real article first and never keeps that consent page as a story's text. Stories that already show the notice will swap in the real article the next time you open them.

13826.title: Android: App crashes if there are no unread items and a feed is selected
13826.note: Play Console top crash for builds 282/283: StackOverflowError in SessionDataSource.getNextNonEmptyFolder (39 reports, 14 users). Recursive next-folder search wrapped forever when no folder had unread feeds. Replaced with a bounded loop; 3 unit tests added, 18 in the class pass. Reply assumes the next Android release ships the fix.
13826.reply: Found it. When you open a feed with nothing unread, the app looks for the next folder that still has unread stories, and if there wasn't one anywhere it kept looping through your folders until it ran out of stack and crashed. It's fixed in the next Android release, which I'll push out shortly. Until then, switching the filter to All Stories avoids it.

13835.title: Cannot add a custom atom feed from bugzilla
13835.deploy: done: make celery + make deploy on 2026-09-17 (c499209b6)
13835.note: bugs.kde.org 403s any User-Agent carrying a desktop browser string (Chrome any version, Firefox < 140) and serves non-browser UAs; verified with curl and from happ-web-01 with the feed's own headers (default and fake UA 403, plain UA 200). FetchFeed only retried with the fake browser UA, then the budget-gated ScrapingBee fallback; the plain UA lived only in fetch_forbidden. Prod feed 10310393 exists (subscriber is NewsBlur user 'sup', created Sep 15 with one proxy success, 403 since). Fix: plain-UA retry after a 401/403/406/451/503 in the main chain; also fixed the falsy-Response guard that gave real 429s the fake-UA retry. End-to-end proven locally on the exact URL (feed 32704: 0 stories/[Untitled] -> 100 entries/'Bug List'). One Codex round, resolved. Reply assumes deploy. Merged (after resolving the appended-test-class conflict with #2137) and deployed 2026-09-17. Task deploy first failed on all 17 hosts: Android_15.0.0 tag was moved on GitHub and the workers held the old one; Sam approved deleting the stale local tag on the task group, then both deploys passed. Prod feed 10310393 picks the fix up on its next scheduled fetch.
13835.reply: The URL is fine and NewsBlur did find the feed. The fetch was what failed: bugs.kde.org refuses any request whose user agent looks like a desktop browser, and NewsBlur's fetcher ends its user agent with one, so every fetch came back 403 and the feed sat empty with no title. I've changed the fetcher to retry with its plain NewsBlur user agent when a site does that, which bugs.kde.org accepts. Your subscription should fill in on its next fetch after the deploy, no need to re-add it.

13840.title: iPhone Cache Not Deleted
13840.note: Reproduced iOS cleanup defects with isolated NB Alpha database tests: low unread counts skip pruning, cached_text is missed, VACUUM runs before deletion. User chose unread priority with recent read stories in remaining quota and maximum manual compaction. Fix added to existing branch at explicit user request. Reply assumes merge and inclusion in the next iOS release; not yet released or posted. Validation and current-head CI/review results are recorded in PR #2079.
13840.reply:
There is a Delete offline stories button under Preferences → Offline Stories, but I found bugs in both that button and automatic cleanup. Cached article text was being left behind, and deleting stories wasn't shrinking the database file.

I've fixed those for the next iOS update. Manual deletion will clear the cached stories, text, and images and reclaim the disk space. Automatic cleanup will respect your Stories to store limit, prioritizing unread stories and keeping recent read stories only in the remaining space. Your subscriptions and pending read or saved story changes are preserved.
